title: Compliance Sync Runbook & Audit Support Manifest
content:
Purpose:
This runbook is the working artifact for supporting the Crescent Health Systems POC (internal codename: CRESCENT) from a compliance and audit-evidence perspective. It is intended to be used by solutions engineering, the security review team, and the customer security contact during workshop sessions and follow-up evidence collection.

Scope and context:
- Customer: Crescent Health Systems (CHS) — PHI-sensitive workloads evaluated for a Dedicated deployment.
- Objective: produce a prioritized evidence bundle and a deployment checklist that supports CHS internal audit and third-party assessment for initial go/no-go.
- Not in scope: Formal SOC2 audit (this is POC-level evidence and controls mapping).

High-level summary (one paragraph):
We ran an initial security workshop with CHS on 2025-10-20. The customer needs evidence demonstrating: encryption in transit and at rest, KMS key lifecycle, network isolation in Dedicated, data residency guarantees, access control & RBAC, and operational incident logs for a 90-day lookback. This doc captures the artifacts we will produce, the owner for each item, a minimal acceptable evidence template, unresolved gaps, and a 6-week delivery timeline for the full pack.

Artifacts to produce (minimal acceptable evidence, owner, status):
- KMS-key-rotation-log (owner: Priya Desai) — status: collecting; template: audit export CSV with timestamps, key IDs, rotation schedule entries.
- Network-architecture-diagram (owner: Gregory Moore) — status: draft; template: Visio/PDF showing VPCs, subnets, NAT, Private control plane endpoints, peering links.
- Dedicated-deployment-config.yaml (owner: Evan Chen) — status: in_progress; template: redwood dedicated manifest with annotations for isolation controls and autoscale policy.
- Host hardening checklist snapshot (owner: Leah Ramirez) — status: ready; template: checklist + baseline AMI build ID + STIG/benchmarks applied.
- Access-review-export (owner: Sandra Kline) — status: pending; template: CSV of IAM principals with last login, roles, MFA flag.
- Audit-log-sample (owner: Priya Desai) — status: collecting; template: sample 7-day event stream (JSONL) redacted for customer PII.
- Pen-test findings summary (owner: vendor-psc) — status: scheduled; template: executive summary + remediation RAG.

Control mapping (short):
- Data encryption at rest: evidence = KMS-key-rotation-log, storage policy, config snippet showing SSE enabled.
- Network segmentation: evidence = Network-architecture-diagram, VPC flow log sample, firewall rules export.
- Access control: evidence = Access-review-export, RBAC matrix, SSO integration config (SAML metadata).
- Logging & monitoring: evidence = Audit-log-sample, alerting rule snapshots, retention policy doc.
- Change management: evidence = Deployment runbook + git commit hashes for infra changes.

Workshop recap (2025-10-20):
Attendees: CHS security (Tom Hale, Anika R.), Redwood solutions (Leah, Greg, Priya), infra engineer (Evan).
Key outcomes:
- CHS requires HSM-backed KMS for production; POC can use cloud KMS with planned HSM migration path.
- Must demonstrate data residency within us-east-2 for seed dataset.
- CHS asked for a 48-hour incident response contact SLA and an explanation of forensic artifacts we can provide.

Open questions for CHS (to resolve in next workshop):
1) Are there any third-party processors we need to list explicitly in the evidence bundle?
2) Confirm the scope of PHI — full PII vs hashed identifiers only.
3) Acceptable redaction rules for audit logs (PII removal).

Short-term delivery plan (6 weeks):
Week 1: finalize templates and collect KMS rotation metadata + network diagram.
Week 2: produce access-export and run host hardening snapshot.
Week 3: sample audit logs (redacted) and retention policy docs.
Week 4: coordinate pen-test engagement and gather remediation plan.
Week 5: assemble evidence bundle and internal QA.
Week 6: deliver to CHS, live review, and iterate on gaps.

Acceptance criteria for CHS (POC exit):
- Evidence bundle covers the control mapping above with signed owner attestations.
- No critical findings unresolved for production by CHS risk team (critical = direct PHI exposure or encryption disabled).
- Demonstrated end-to-end Dedicated deployment in us-east-2 with network isolation validated via test harness.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: KMS HSM requirement for production delays timeline. Mitigation: produce architectural migration plan and compensating controls (short-term HSM-backed key escrow demo with vendor).
- Risk: log redaction reduces forensics utility. Mitigation: provide side-by-side redacted + truncated raw sample under NDA.

Evidence delivery format and naming convention (must match CHS intake):
- File naming: CRESCENT_evidence_<control>_<YYYYMMDD>.<ext>
- Index file: CRESCENT_evidence_index.csv (columns: artifact_id, control_ref, owner, file_name, sha256, created_at, notes)
- Archive: CRESCENT_evidence_bundle_<timestamp>.tar.gz (signed + checksum)

Owner responsibilities (short):
- Leah Ramirez: runbook owner, curator of index, liaison to CHS security.
- Priya Desai: kms + logs evidence collection and redaction.
- Gregory Moore: network diagrams, flow logs, VPC validation steps.
- Evan Chen: Dedicated deployment manifests and infra-level proofs (git refs, commit links).
- Sandra Kline: access/export and RBAC attestations.

Communication and coordination notes:
- Primary channel: #sec-crescent-poc (Slack). Use threads per artifact (prefix: artifact-<short-id>).
- Use the Confluence page (linked above) as the source of truth for templates; update this doc with any divergence.
- All artifacts intended for external submission must be approved by Leah and have a checksum recorded in the index file.

Next steps (immediate):
- Priya to deliver a sample KMS export by 2025-10-22.
- Gregory to upload the first network diagram draft by 2025-10-23.
- Schedule follow-up with CHS for 1-week demo & evidence review on 2025-10-29.

Notes to self / working items: (informal)
- Make sure the index includes a column marking whether the artifact is redacted or original.
- Need a small script to compute sha256 and attach to index automatically — file: scripts/compute-sha256.py (todo).
- Consider adding a short video walkthrough for the Dedicated demo to reduce back-and-forth with CHS security.

Appendix: minimal evidence templates (quick):
- KMS rotation CSV header: key_id, region, created_at, last_rotated_at, rotation_policy, rotation_owner
- Access export CSV header: principal_id, principal_type, role, last_auth_time, mfa_enabled, source_ip_last_login
- Audit-log sample: JSONL with timestamp, event_type, principal, resource, action, request_id (PII redacted)

If anything in this runbook conflicts with team playbooks (e.g., playbook: incident-response-2025), flag it in the #sec-crescent-poc channel and assign SEC-4983.

Document history (quick):
- 2025-10-15: initial draft (Leah)
- 2025-10-20: post-workshop updates (Greg, Priya)
- 2025-11-07: added evidence naming and index template (Leah)
- 2026-02-28: refreshed timeline and moved pen-test date (final edits prior to submission)
